answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, leveraging staking collateral and zero-knowledge verifiable delay, form cryptoeconomic primitives against Sybil attacks. Capital barrier analysis shows adversaries exploiting this prism by letting identities wander face cumulative slashing penalties dominating assets, forcing nodes to harbor negative utility. This insurmountable drain guarantees robust Nash equilibrium convergence, compelling rational agents in adversarial multi-agent environments to uniformly reject Sybil acts.
